title: Local lci duality and scalar-equivariant Ext identification
statement:
For a morphism $p:X\to S$, a nonnegative integer $d$, an open $U\subset X$ and a polynomial presentation $C$ of relative rank $d$ [def-sfb-flat-lci-adjunction-system], write $i:U\to P$, $n=c+d$, and $L_C=(\bigwedge^c C_{U/P})^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^n i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$ for its specified adjunction line. For any $\mathcal O_U$-module $M$ and endomorphism $s$ of $\mathcal O_U$, define the scalar action $s_M:M\to M$ by the left-unitor inverse, $s\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$, and the left unitor, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

The predicate $C.\mathrm{HasDualityModel}$ says that for every derived-category instance at the standard universe $u+1$ on modules on $P$ [def-pc-derived-category], there exists an isomorphism in that ambient category
$$i_*L_C[d]\simeq R\mathcal Hom_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S}[n]),$$
using the actual direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every endomorphism $s$ of $\mathcal O_U$, the isomorphism intertwines the shifted direct image of $s_{L_C}$ with the contravariant action of $i_*s$ on the first Hom argument. The predicate $C.\mathrm{HasExtIdentification}$ likewise says, for every such derived-category instance, that there exists an isomorphism
$$i_*L_C\simeq\mathcal Ext^c_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S})$$
of ordinary module sheaves, with sheaf Ext defined by [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext], intertwining $i_*s_{L_C}$ with the contravariant functorial action of $i_*s$. Each predicate asserts existence with the displayed closed-source scalar compatibility; neither selects an isomorphism nor imposes any geometric hypothesis beyond the supplied presentation. Specified signed normalizations are additional data, not part of either predicate. For a point $s\in S$, the convenience construction $\mathrm{flatLCIGeometricFibre}(p,s)$ is exactly the geometric fibre of [def-weil-geometric-fibre]: $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}$, formed along the composite of the algebraic-closure inclusion with the canonical residue-field point of $S$. This is the actual Mathlib pullback of those morphisms, and its historical name imposes no flatness or lci hypothesis.
